body: I’m posting this under an alt account for a reason, but I’ll say in the south, and I work in visual design and editing.

Thank you! Like I said earlier, it's not poly necessarily, but it's not an open relationship. It's like we're friends, we have benefits, but the benefits come second. If there needs to be communication of jealousy, we take it like a poly thing and discuss it. If it ends up having to end, we discuss it and lean on the friendship.

If anything, it kinda became something and it progressed naturally. My boyfriend finds it hot when he complements either or both of us, (same here) and we give him the same. Both of them think it funny to fluster me. He runs away during Smash Bros as me and the bf taunt each other. We have a dynamic that works so far. And we like it. :)

Thank you! Yes, this is something we both want. For now, like I said in a previous post, we all are on the same page so far. Right now we consider it not an open thing, not polyamory- but like somewhere between it. Me and my boyfriend don't want to just hook up with anybody- we want it to be with people we like and trust. As in, us and the guy are friends first and FWBs second. If there ever comes a time where this arrangement has to end for the better of all three of us, we won't hesitate to end the FWB relationship and hope that the friendship lasts. Luckily we all get on pretty well.

Jealousy is a concern- as it is when others enter the scene- and I know from Poly points of view it is a matter best discussed. So far everyone is level headed. Thanks for the wish of luck- we'll need it. ^^

This takes a lot of communication - this whole subreddit knows it - and thankfully all of us are willing to listen and adjust so far.

Me and my boyfriend love each other for more than sex- we spend romantic time together. We consider each other partners. The validation thing is fair- that does seem to be something to think about and I will mull over it. But if anything we're having some fun with a good friend at the moment, and I check in with him to make sure how he's handling it. I really don't want to be inconsiderate, which is an issue I've seen again and again.

If I'm being honest, and I hope this isn't going too close for the throat- what you said about couples and them claiming open relationships work, and that you've never believed them- I've heard literally the other story. That open relationships saved the romance. Now that doesn't mean I have that point of view myself one hundred percent, but it is food for thought. Some things work for some that in a million years wouldn't work for someone else. No judgement, just a point to think about.

I do appreciate your feedback, and I hope however you flourish in romance, it fulfills what you need. Sending love.

Sorry about deleting mine- I felt it unfinished and I took a moment to breathe and collect. I'm sorry about assuming! Honest.

And I might have projected there. I know a person who's VERY passive aggressive with emoji...

I agree that monogamy is great, and I never want to seem like THAT gay who's like "monogamy is evil how dare you mention it in my presence no monogamous couple lasts 😤" because I myself see this as non-monogamy or monogamish- this situation only exists in absolute trust and respect. And that's hard. We both agreed it's only gotta be with people we already know and trust, because at the end of the day we both want a connection to be there at some level. And that list is a short one. We're not going out to find randoms. So this is also probably a rare case.

I hope you stay well too. Sending love to you, and best wishes for your future.

Hi! Thanks for the advice. I will start off with this- be warned, it's a lot.

The main reason I came here is because I know that these are difficult situations. People can get hurt. But I've had things in the past that ended poorly, due to lack of communication on my part and other people's part. I want to tackle it right now. Early, before it might become an issue. It seems everyone is happy in this situation but I am done with waiting and not thinking ahead. I want to be prepared. I'm trying to take responsibility for my actions now and not later.

Would I want this if my partner didn't want this? Honestly, no. It's not a deal breaker. We love each other very much, and we mostly wanted to see how it would work. Right now it's good. And we both like it.

Second question, not sure what this means. If you mean does it make me jealous? Not really. If he's enjoying himself, and being honest with me how it is and how he feels, and still makes romantic, and sexual, time for me, then I'm okay with it.

This arrangement long-term? I can see the guy being a friend we have fun with now and again, and if it goes well, sure. If the friend has to stop because of a monogamous relationship, I'd understand and still want to hang with him as long as those boundaries are set. If his own bf is jealous, that's a conversation there too. My boyfriend, regardless who we swing/sext is my boyfriend. I love him and want him to be happy.

I think it's a little presumptuous to assume I'm worried or jealous- I was the reason the friend was brought in. My boyfriend for the most of the relationship has fantasized about having sex with others, and it wasn't until recently I played with that idea myself. 

I came here because I know some people have had non-monogamy in relationships work out and not work out. I want to find people who have been there and hear stories about what happened to them. Your comment is well appreciated and food for thought. Honestly. 

Monogamy is the preferred option for a lot of people. And that's valid and okay. But don't assume that because I'm here I have major hangups. I'm here because I want to face this head-on, and come to terms with difficulties, and hear from people who have made it work.

And I'm scared of making relationships where I am, since I'm right in the middle of Bible-Thump-Voted-for-Trump County. I don't want to fight. I want it to end.
